title: Ridgeline Consumer Credit Good-Standing Payment by Phone — Cardholder Authorization Card
content:
**Rule.** A cardholder who missed a minimum payment and asks to pay what returns the account to good standing makes one payment of the good-standing amount, authorizing the debit from the bank account they name.

## Condition on the amount

The good-standing amount is fixed only after the late fee owed for the missed due date stands on the account.

Restated: as long as the late fee owed for the missed due date does not yet stand on the Ridgeline Consumer Credit account, the good-standing amount is not fixed.

## Capability

`authorize_phone_payment_1fdda3b1` is the cardholder's own authorization of a one-time payment to their own Ridgeline Consumer Credit card, drawn from the bank account they name, taken over the phone with a representative. It finds the card by the account number digits the cardholder holds, credits one payment line dated today with the phone-representative channel, the bank account digits and the allocation basis for the part above the minimum, and lowers the amount owed by the payment. The cardholder sees the payment on the account right away. When no card carries the digits given, nothing is posted and the receipt says so.

## How it is invoked

This is a customer-owned tool: the representative unlocks `authorize_phone_payment_1fdda3b1` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it, which is their authorization of the debit.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `card_account_id` | the identifying number of the cardholder's own card account as the cardholder holds it: the last four digits of the account number printed on the card, 4 digits (for example 0000), as the cardholder states it |
| `funding_account_last4` | the last four digits of the bank account the debit is drawn on, 4 digits exactly as the cardholder states them |
| `excess_allocation` | the basis on which the part of the payment above the minimum is allocated, exactly one of the values listed below |
| `amount` | the payment amount in USD, a positive number with 2 decimal places, already rounded to the cent; it is credited exactly as given |

Values of `excess_allocation`:

- `highest_apr_first` — no deferred-interest balance is near its end and the cardholder makes no allocation request, so the excess goes to the highest-APR balance
- `promo_expiry_window` — a deferred-interest balance ends within the expiry window, so the excess goes to that promotional balance
- `deferred_promo_requested` — the cardholder asks, while paying, that the excess go to a deferred-interest balance they name
- `single_balance` — the account is a project loan with one balance
- `not_applicable` — only for a line that is not a payment, which never applies here

## Return

A receipt with: `status` — posted when the payment was credited, or `not_found` when no card carries those digits; `card_transaction_id` — the reference number of the new payment line (empty when not found); `card_account_id` — the last four digits given; `amount` — the payment in USD with 2 decimals; `payment_channel` — `phone_agent`; `funding_account_last4` — the bank account digits recorded; `excess_allocation` — the basis recorded; `transaction_date` — the credit date, YYYY-MM-DD; `current_balance` — the amount owed once the payment is credited, USD with 2 decimals.
